description: Migrate the remaining five hand-rolled agent-spec reads that are NOT name->model scans onto the hardened reader, preserving each caller's current failure semantics exactly (skip-and-continue everywhere here; a refused spec must degrade like an absent one). Sites: agent.py migrate_agent_specs (reads AND rewrites — the copy-out case _spec_path_is_safe warns about); dashboard/handlers/agents.py two glob-scan reads; dashboard/handlers/mcp.py three agents-dir scan reads. Depends on nothing in FEAT-001 (independent), but touches disjoint code so the two features can land in either order.
steps: src/kiro_crew/agent.py `migrate_agent_specs` (~2652-2673): this reads each spec, strips bookkeeping keys, and REWRITES it in place via `_atomic_json_write`. Replace `data = json.loads(spec_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))` + the `except (OSError, ValueError): continue` + `if not isinstance(data, dict): continue` with `data = _read_spec_capped(spec_path)` (the existing wrapper at ~2704 that calls _read_agent_spec) and `if data is None: continue`. CRITICAL — the rewrite path: _read_agent_spec refuses a symlink whose RESOLVED target is sensitive, but the copy-out hazard _spec_path_is_safe documents (following ANY symlink reads the target and writes a modified copy into the agents dir) is broader. Because this site writes back, guard the rewrite with the existing `_spec_path_is_safe(spec_path, agents_dir)` fence BEFORE reading/rewriting (agents_dir = kiro_agents_dir_path()), skipping (continue) any path that is a symlink, escapes the dir, or is sensitive — matching how the other rewrite paths (~2784, ~2836) already gate on _spec_path_is_safe. Net: read through the hardened reader AND keep the stricter no-symlink-at-all fence for the write. Preserve the `cleaned` counter, the name/stem fallback (`data.get('name') or spec_path.stem`), the per-file `_atomic_json_write` try/except OSError warning, and the return value.

src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/agents.py `_namespaced_agent_file_exists` (~93-107): replace `data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))` inside the `glob('*--{agent_name}.json')` loop and its `except (OSError, ValueError): continue` with `data = _read_agent_spec(path)` + `if data is None: continue`, then keep the `if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get('name') == agent_name: return True` check (data is already a dict when non-None, but leaving the isinstance check is harmless; prefer `if data.get('name') == agent_name`). Import `_read_agent_spec` from kiro_crew.agent_discovery (add to the existing `from kiro_crew.agent_discovery import (...)` block that already pulls spec_model/spec_str). Preserve the outer `except OSError: return False` and the trailing `return False`.

src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/agents.py delete/patch scan (~1565-1570): replace `data = json.loads(f.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))` inside `for f in kiro_agents_dir_path().glob('*.json')` with `data = _read_agent_spec(f)` + `if data is None: continue` placed BEFORE the `if data.get('name') == name or f.stem == name:` match. Preserve the surrounding try/except structure and all the delete/patch branch logic that follows the match unchanged (this is a large block — only the read line and the None-skip change).

src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/mcp.py `_collect_server_rows` (~781-783): replace `spec = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))` inside `for path in sorted(agents_dir.glob('*.json'))` + `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError): continue` + `if not isinstance(spec, dict): continue` with `spec = _read_agent_spec(path)` + `if spec is None: continue`. Keep the `agent_name = spec.get('name') or path.stem` and mcpServers extraction unchanged. Add `_read_agent_spec` to the imports from kiro_crew.agent_discovery (or import agent_discovery and call ad._read_agent_spec — match whatever import style this module already uses; it imports kiro_agents_dir_path from kiro_crew.agent).

src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/mcp.py `_launch_specs_for` (~2692-2694): same replacement pattern as the previous step (glob '*.json', read via _read_agent_spec, `if spec is None: continue`, drop the now-redundant `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError)` and `isinstance` non-dict check). Preserve the `if name not in names` filtering and SimpleNamespace construction.

src/kiro_crew/dashboard/handlers/mcp.py third agents-dir scan (~2755-2760): same replacement pattern. Re-grep to confirm this is an agents-dir `*.json` spec read and NOT a `_GLOBAL_MCP_JSON` or `_installed_agent_config()` read (those are OUT OF SCOPE). Preserve surrounding logic and skip-and-continue semantics.

Do NOT touch: any `_GLOBAL_MCP_JSON.read_text` read in mcp.py, the `_installed_agent_config()` reads at ~258/~381, or reads at agents.py ~512 / mcp.py ~1636/~2449/~2620 unless a re-grep shows they are agents-dir spec reads in the seven-site set — the task scope is exactly the enumerated agent-spec reads in the user-writable agents dir.

Add tests. In test/test_agent_specs_migration (new module test/test_migrate_agent_specs.py or extend an existing agent test module): cover migrate_agent_specs skipping an oversized spec (monkeypatch hooks.MAX_FILE_BYTES) and refusing to rewrite through a symlink (requires_symlinks; assert the symlink target is unchanged and the count excludes it). For the dashboard handlers, add focused tests (new test/test_dashboard_agent_spec_reads.py) that: _namespaced_agent_file_exists returns False (not raise) for an oversized/non-utf8 namespaced file and does not read a symlink-to-sensitive; _collect_server_rows / _launch_specs_for skip an oversized/non-object spec instead of raising. Mirror the fixture and monkeypatch patterns in test/test_agent_discovery.py and test/test_cli_doctor.py. If a dashboard handler needs the agents dir redirected, use the same fake_home/KIROCREW_HOME mechanism the existing dashboard tests use (check test/ for an existing dashboard handler test to copy the app/state setup).
Run host verification: py_compile + ruff check + ruff format --check on all changed/added files.
acceptance_criteria: None of the five sites (agent.py migrate_agent_specs; agents.py _namespaced_agent_file_exists and the delete/patch scan; mcp.py _collect_server_rows, _launch_specs_for, and the third agents-dir scan) contains `json.loads(...read_text(...))` for an agents-dir spec anymore; each reads via _read_agent_spec (or _read_spec_capped in agent.py).

migrate_agent_specs still gates its in-place rewrite on _spec_path_is_safe so a symlink is not followed for the copy-out, and still returns the count of cleaned specs; a refused/oversized spec is skipped, not fatal.

Every migrated site preserves skip-and-continue semantics: a None/refused spec is treated exactly like an absent one (continue / return False / degrade to empty), introducing no new raise or fatal path.
_GLOBAL_MCP_JSON reads and _installed_agent_config() reads are untouched (out of scope).
New dashboard/migration tests assert oversized, non-utf8/AppleDouble, non-object, and symlink-to-sensitive inputs are skipped rather than raising.
py_compile and ruff check/format --check pass on all changed files.
